definition: In the context of decision trees in information theory and machine learning, information gain refers to the conditional expected value of the Kullback–Leibler divergence of the univariate probability distribution of one variable from the conditional distribution of this variable given the other one.
details: (In broader contexts, information gain can also be used as a synonym for either Kullback–Leibler divergence or mutual information, but the focus of this article is on the more narrow meaning below.) Explicitly, the information gain of a random variable X {\displaystyle X} obtained from an observation of a random variable A {\displaystyle A} taking value a {\displaystyle a} is defined as: I G ( X , a ) = D KL ( P X ∣ a ∥ P X ) {\displaystyle {\mathit {IG}}(X,a)=D_{\text{KL}}{\bigl (}P_{X\mid a}\parallel P_{X}{\bigr )}} In other words, it is the Kullback–Leibler divergence of P X ( x ) {\displaystyle P_{X}(x)} (the prior distribution for X {\displaystyle X} ) from P X ∣ a ( x ) {\displaystyle P_{X\mid a}(x)} (the posterior distribution for X {\displaystyle X} given A = a {\displaystyle A=a} ). The expected value of the information gain is the mutual information I ( X ; A ) {\displaystyle I(X;A)} : E A ⁡ [ I G ( X , A ) ] = I ( X ; A ) {\displaystyle \operatorname {E} _{A}[{\mathit {IG}}(X,A)]=I(X;A)} i.e. the reduction in the entropy of X {\displaystyle X} achieved by learning the state of the random variable A {\displaystyle A} . explainer.lead: Information gain measures how much observing a variable reduces uncertainty about another, and in decision trees it is used to choose splits. It matters because it turns the choice of split into a principled information-theoretic quantity.

tiers.eli5: Before asking a question you guess the answer is 50/50; after asking, the answer is nearly certain. The information gain is how much that question sharpened your guess.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a splitting criterion, picking the attribute whose observation most reduces uncertainty about the target. A pitfall is that gain can favor variables with many values, so it is often paired with normalization or other criteria.
tiers.paperLevel: Information gain of random variable X from observing variable A taking value a is IG(X,a) = D_KL(P_{X|a} || P_X), the conditional expected value of the Kullback–Leibler divergence of the univariate distribution of one variable from its conditional distribution given the other. In broader contexts it is used as a synonym for KL divergence or mutual information.

explainer.example: If before an observation X is split evenly between two classes and after observing a = yes X is almost certainly one class, the KL divergence between those distributions is the gain for that split.
